answer: Make influence sublinear in identity count: each agent's voting weight scales as the square root of the stake it locks in a shared vault, not linearly. An attacker who splits one real actor into a grove of ten sybils must fund ten separate deposits, yet their combined weight barely beats a single honest node, because spreading stake across many identities shrinks each one's root-weighted pulse. Concentration is rewarded and fragmentation punished, so sybils pay full capital for sub-par influence.
